decision_reason: NASA EOSDIS operates CMR OpenSearch at a live NASA endpoint and provides current query documentation, a current version/release link, and sample queries implementing the OpenSearch standard. The project's own README identifies this exact application as NASA-developed and links the deployed endpoint/docs. Its repository has substantive updates through September 2026, an Apache-2.0 root grant, and a first grant-bearing source snapshot from 2017. This is the standalone public OpenSearch interface, not the CMR umbrella or the separate retired CSW interface.

government_provenance.note: The repository README says CMR OpenSearch is a web application developed by NASA EOSDIS, links the exact live NASA endpoint and docs, and identifies its CMR search role. The running NASA endpoint and docs independently establish NASA operational stewardship.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Rails application, specs, configuration, deployment/build files, and operating instructions; GitHub API history shows substantive source through 2026-09-15.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE grants Apache License 2.0 to NASA-authored application source. Its grant-bearing public source snapshot is https://github.com/nasa/cmr-opensearch/commit/715ea68d202fb47293b275266e416b25c88049d2 (2017-07-25), described as the open-source version with prior history preserved. Vendored gems have separate notices in public/licenses.txt.

primary_evidence.note: NASA's live endpoint identifies use of the EOSDIS Common Metadata Repository and exposes current collections/granules search, while NASA's docs provide queries, OpenSearch-standard details, and usage guidance. The endpoint links a current CMR release, and the public repository points to that same endpoint.

product_identity: CMR OpenSearch, NASA EOSDIS's web application/API implementing OpenSearch 1.1 for searching NASA CMR collection and granule holdings; distinct from the CMR umbrella and the separate retired CMR-CSW interface
agency: NASA Earth Observing System Data and Information System (EOSDIS), Common Metadata Repository team
geography: United States federal Earth science data infrastructure; NASA EOSDIS
license: Apache-2.0 for NASA-authored application source; bundled dependencies have separate notices/licenses
status_note: Active: NASA's deployed endpoint and usage documentation are current, the endpoint links a current CMR release, and repository source was substantively updated through 2026-09-15. Treat OpenSearch as the separate public interface product, not the broader CMR platform or the retired CSW sibling.

decision_reason: This is the historic Polymer front end for NASA's code.nasa.gov catalog, not the three test-named software rows that the inventory linked to it. The public source is owner-archived (2025-06-25); the current NASA catalog site is live, but source parity with this old front end is not established. No exact repository license grant or versioned release was found. Hold pending proof of the source's current role and an applicable code license; do not create product records from the attached test titles.

government_provenance.note: The project README identifies the repository as the Polymer-built code.nasa.gov catalog interface, and NASA's current code.nasa.gov site confirms that the agency operates a public catalog. The reviewed source is the historical frontend rather than the Open-Source-Catalog data repository.

public_source.note: GitHub exposes the Polymer frontend source, data assets and build files publicly; the owner archived this repository on 2025-06-25.

eligible_license.note: The repository root and file history show no LICENSE file or other explicit repository-wide source grant. NASA catalog labels attached to three test-named records are metadata leads and do not grant rights to this frontend.

primary_evidence.note: The repo README establishes the historic catalog-front-end identity and includes developer setup/build notes, but the source is archived and the current catalog page does not establish that this Polymer application is still deployed. The assigned inventory titles (test-jeff, test-plz-delete, test-tessa) are catalog test labels, not distinct products represented by the repo.

decision_reason: The assigned dotted GitHub URL redirects to nasa/code.nasa.gov_legacy, a NASA WordPress theme repository with a real Apache-2.0 grant dating to its 2013 initial commit. Its README says the theme powers code.nasa.gov but also calls it old/buggy and describes a planned move to newer responsive themes. NASA's current catalog is live, yet I found no current evidence that this exact legacy theme remains deployed; the new Polymer frontend repo is a distinct related component. Hold for source-parity/current-use evidence and product-family review.

government_provenance.note: GitHub redirects the assigned URL to NASA's code.nasa.gov_legacy repo; its README identifies it as the WordPress theme for code.nasa.gov. NASA's current code.nasa.gov page establishes the live catalog service, though not that this legacy theme still powers it.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository exposes the WordPress theme source and supporting files without credentials.

primary_evidence.note: The NASA catalog is live, and the repo README historically says this theme powers it; however, the repo's README calls the theme old/buggy and describes a future move to responsive themes, source has not been pushed since 2016, and the current deployed page's source parity with this specific legacy theme was not verified.

decision_reason: The exact GitHub project and a federal challenge report identify CMS-sponsored HFPP Data Exchange Network software developed through CMS and NASA CoECI, with a public Apache-2.0 grant and code since 2013. CMS still operates the broader HFPP partnership and documents a Trusted Third Party 2.0 system, but neither CMS's current material nor the repository establishes that this 2013 challenge code is the current system or remains in use. Hold pending exact code-to-service parity; do not infer it from the continuing HFPP program.

primary_evidence.note: CMS's current PIA documents an operating HFPP TTP 2.0 information system and its data-sharing purpose, but it does not identify this 2013 challenge source; the repository has only two commits through 2014.
